summary: A leader puts a bill directly on the calendar when referral would leave it with a hostile chair.
realLife: Mansfield bypassed Eastland’s Judiciary Committee to get the House civil rights bill before the Senate.
gates: The chamber permits direct placement on its calendar.
inGame: bill-held-in-committee identifies a chair's hold. needs: a procedural choice to bypass referral before a chair obtains the bill.

turns.what: The leader sends the bill to committee after the chair commits to a hearing date.
turns.pulledBy: The chair gives a public undertaking before referral.
turns.writesBack: The bill enters committee with a date members can check.

turns.what: The chamber sends one question to committee and keeps the rest before it.
turns.pulledBy: Members want a record on a narrow provision without delaying the entire bill.
turns.writesBack: The referral covers only the named question.
